note: Generated by design/tools/bosses_7_10.py. World units. The page design/bosses/reprise.md is made from this data.
name: Kaleidos, Reprise
key: A minor: First Light's chords and lead

common.arrives: on the last Drop of its Track and stays until it is dead; the music holds its Drop for the whole fight
common.health: the number given is a first guess: tune it with the careful bot until the fight lasts what the page says with the build a player has by then, as was done for Longwave and The Choir; x (1 + 0.5 per extra player)
common.grid: everything it does lands on the song's grid and is computed from the song's clock, so every device in a co-op run sees the same fight with nothing new on the wire
common.reward: a bonus Trio and Shards for each player; the Track ends
common.crowd: half of the Drop's crowd, fodder only, unless the page says otherwise

parts.name: The wheel
parts.what: Kaleidos as built, a quarter larger: a core of radius 80 and six arms 300 wu long. Each arm takes the accent colour of the Track whose boss it plays: Ultraviolet, Solar, Reef, Aurora, Furnace, Zenith

parts.name: The soloist
parts.what: The arm whose turn it is: at 3.0 with its white core line, a pool of its colour under it, the other arms at 1.0

damageScale.note: wherever the page says a part cannot be hurt yet it takes a quarter; in the Medley the closed core's quarter goes to the soloist's sixth

numbers.turn: one revolution every eight bars; it keeps 450 to 650 wu from the nearest player as Kaleidos does
numbers.armShare: in the Medley each arm has a sixth of that phase's health

phases.name: Reprise
rules: Kaleidos's own fight at 174: mirrored fans of five from each pair of arms, now on the two-step's hits (kick on steps 0 and 10, snare on 4 and 12) instead of the eighths
The arms cannot be hurt yet (they are white-edged); the core is open, x 1, and x 2 on the One

phases.name: Medley
rules: The core closes. The arms take turns round the wheel, two bars each; the soloist is the only thing that can be hurt, and a dead arm's solo is skipped from then on
Kaleidos's arm: its mirrored fans on the eighths
Longwave's arm: it lets go as a wave of eight segments that crosses the frame once; only the crests can be hurt
The Choir's arm: a volley on the One, answered on three by the arm opposite
Event Horizon's arm: for its two bars ships and bullets are drawn toward the wheel at 200 wu/s, and a ring of twenty-four leaves the core on its second bar line
Polyrhythm's arm: two rings a bar with a gap each, one on three pulses and one on four; the gaps meet on the One
Feedback's arm: an Echo of the nearest player replays that player's last bar from the far side of the wheel

phases.name: Last Light
rules: The bare core. It fires First Light's arpeggio: one bullet on every sixteenth, its direction 15 degrees round for every semitone the note stands above the bar's lowest, the whole figure turning 45 degrees a bar, 260 wu/s
x 1, and x 2 on the One. Over this phase the palette cross-fades from Last Light to Ultraviolet

weakPoint: the core on the One in the first and last phases; the soloist in the Medley
death: no burst: the core dims to a point, one white ripple crosses the whole lattice, and the ENCORE card comes up over First Light. The largest reward of the run
sound: Each solo is in its boss's own voice: Kaleidos's bells, Longwave's rubber string, a pad voice for The Choir, the sub drop for Event Horizon, toms three against four for Polyrhythm, the player's lead reversed for Feedback
A dead arm takes its voice out of the medley
The last pattern is First Light's arpeggio on the P3 bell, doubled by the band's lead: the tune of the first minute, at 174
Death: the tonic held, the ripple a reversed cymbal ending on the encore's first downbeat
caps: one wheel, eight wave segments, one Echo, 200 bullets
